While all their peers have merged mutual funds with their main app, zerodha wont because they don’t want a super app! This app is so basic and so limited features: - no option for creating daily SIP - no option to sort on XIRR - no option to model gains or STCG/LTCG! - customers don’t mean anything to them as they are discount brokers!! - Give any suggestion to them and they are like “we are the largest broker, so take what you get and shut up!” - Separate app for mutual funds, no other broker does that! If you ask why, their answer is same as above! - Unjustified charges! Delivery trades are free but they charge for buy back orders, which are delivery orders! Similarly if you apply for a buy offer of a company, they charge even if the order is not accepted! If you ask why, the answer is again same as above! - The DP charge is 300/- per annum, and they say that it’s to be charged quarterly like any other broker! But they charge it every 90 days, in their calculations 90 days * 4 = 1 year! Don’t ask why, you will get the same answer as above!

- shameless and unethical advertising of mutual funds from their own company

review_title: Overcomplicated redesign is ruining a once-simple app
review_text:
As a long-time Upstox user, I am extremely disappointed with the direction this app is heading. I am not a daily day trader; I simply invest manage my portfolio, invest, and close the app until the next time. Upstox used to be great for this, but the recent design changes have turned a once-clean platform into a cluttered mess.
In the name of "upgrading," they have made basic navigation unnecessarily complicated. Finding standard services and essential portfolio details takes way too much effort now. The home page is crowded with irrelevant features that many of us never asked for:
 Unsolicited F&O & Strategy Tools: Pushing complex options trading strategies and trade ideas directly onto the homepage clutter is useless for long-term investors. Anyone who actively trades F&O already knows what tools they need; forcing it on everyone else just creates noise.
 Intrusive "Expert Advice" & Mutual Fund SIPs: Putting aggressive recommendations front and center makes the app feel cheap and chaotic. If someone wants to start a Mutual Fund SIP, they will intentionally navigate to the MF section—it doesn't need to take over the main screen.
Upstox needs to realize that adding more clutter isn't an upgrade—it's bad UX. Making the app hard to understand for simple, long-term investors will only drive customers away. If this bloated interface continues to prioritize pushed features over clean usability, I will consider closing my Demat account and shifting my portfolio to a simpler competitor.

review_title: Feature Request: Transform INDmoney into a Complete Wealth Operating System
review_text:
I’ve been using INDmoney extensively and I believe it is already one of the best wealth aggregation platforms in India. The ability to track bank accounts, investments, net worth, family accounts, Indian stocks, US stocks, mutual funds, EPF, NPS and other assets in one place is extremely valuable.

However, there is a major opportunity to evolve INDmoney from a wealth tracker into a complete Personal Wealth Operating System.

Key feature gaps I would love to see:

1. Custom Transaction Categorization

* Allow users to create their own Categories and Subcategories.
* Example: Income → Salary, Bonus, Dividend.
* Expense → Food, Travel, Medical, Shopping.
* Investment → Mutual Fund SIP, Stock Purchase, Gold Purchase.

2. Full Budgeting System

* Monthly Budget vs Actual.
* Category-wise spending analysis.
* Savings rate and investment rate tracking.
* Cash flow forecasting.

3. Money Flow Tracking

* Track complete money movement across accounts.
* Example:
 Savings Account → INDmoney Wallet → USD Conversion → US Stock Purchase → Sale → Wallet → Bank Account.
* Every rupee and dollar should have a traceable journey.

4. Account Management Hub

* Maintain all bank accounts, broker accounts, wallet accounts and important account information.
* Track balances automatically from transactions.

5. Advanced Portfolio Rebalancing

* User-defined target allocation.
* Show current allocation vs target allocation.
* Recommend exact buy/sell actions.
* Tax-efficient rebalancing using future contributions.

6. Portfolio Drift Monitoring

* Alert users when allocations drift beyond a chosen threshold.
* Example: Equity target 60%, current 70%.

7. Financial Health Score

* Score based on:
 * Savings rate
 * Emergency fund
 * Diversification
 * Debt levels
 * Goal progress
 * Asset allocation
* Provide actionable recommendations.

8. Goal Planning

* Retirement
* House Purchase
* Child Education
* Vacation
* Emergency Fund

Show target amount, current progress and projected completion date.

9. Financial Independence Dashboard

* FI/FIRE progress tracker.
* Passive income tracking.
* Years to financial independence.
* Required corpus calculations.

10. More Powerful Web Platform
 The web app has huge potential.
 Please consider:

* Custom dashboards
* Drag-and-drop widgets
* Advanced portfolio analytics
* Portfolio drill-down reports
* Exportable reports
* Multi-monitor friendly layouts
* Professional investor dashboards

11. Multi-Currency Reporting
 Many users invest globally.
 Allow users to choose a Master Reporting Currency (INR, USD, EUR, GBP, etc.) and see net worth, gains, allocations and reports automatically converted.
12. AI Wealth Coach using MCP
 Since INDmoney already supports Claude MCP, allow users to ask:

* Am I overallocated anywhere?
* How should I invest ₹50,000 this month?
* What is my biggest portfolio risk?
* What should I do to improve my financial health score?

INDmoney already aggregates data better than most competitors. Adding budgeting, cash flow, rebalancing, financial planning and financial independence tracking could make it the definitive personal finance platform for serious investors.

review_title: ⚠️ Beware! ET Money is a Trap – My Investing Nightmare 😡🚨
review_text:
ET Money is by far the worst investment app I have ever come across. I initially trusted the platform and invested over ₹1 lakh across 8 SIPs, planning for long-term investments. However, for the last four months, every single SIP has failed, despite having more than sufficient funds in my bank account.
During the bull market, the app was quick to accept my investments. But now, in a bear phase—when investing makes the most sense—all my SIPs are getting rejected. I contacted their customer support multiple times, but instead of resolving the issue, they kept shifting blame—first to the UPI app, then to my bank. However, both my bank and UPI app confirmed that they never received any charge requests from ET Money during this period. This clearly shows that the issue is entirely on ET Money's end, especially since my other SIPs are working perfectly fine with other investment apps. To make matters worse, their customer support has now completely stopped responding to my emails.
Adding to the frustration, there is no proper desktop site for making investments. If you visit their website, they force you to download the mobile app to access your account. When I installed the app and tried investing manually via lump sum, there was no option to do so! In fact, I couldn’t even access detailed information about my investments. Every feature is locked behind a paywall, constantly pushing their premium subscription. Without it, the app is practically useless—you can’t even access your own investments!
I strongly advise against using ET Money if you value your hard-earned money and mental peace. The app might look sleek, but it’s completely worthless unless you pay for their premium plan. Now, I’m stuck—I can't invest, I can't track my funds properly, and withdrawing would mean exit load charges, tax implications, and potential losses due to the current market downturn.
ET Money’s customer support is a joke, and the app is nothing but a trap to force users into their paid plans. Avoid this app at all costs! 🚨

review_title: The app does not show a portfolio-level “Invested vs Current Value” time-based chart
review_text:
Paytm Money is a good investment app overall. SIP execution is smooth, data is accurate, and the interface is clean and easy to use.

However, there is one major missing feature that becomes frustrating for long-term investors.

👉 The app does not show a portfolio-level “Invested vs Current Value” time-based chart.
Only individual mutual fund charts are available, but there is no combined portfolio growth chart to visually track how the entire portfolio has grown over time.

While numbers like invested amount, returns, and XIRR are shown,
visualizing the portfolio journey is not possible, which is important for understanding performance and making better decisions.

Apps like Groww and Zerodha already provide this feature.
Paytm Money should add a portfolio growth chart to improve the long-term investing experience.

With this improvement, the app can become much stronger.
